 Inspiration 

 As AI agents like OpenAI and Anthropic become more capable, they can do more than answer questions. They can call APIs, use web tools, modify data, make purchases, send messages, and take other real-world actions. 

 This creates a simple problem: 

 
 An agent having access to a tool does not mean the human gave it permission to use that tool. 
 

 I built MIRROR as a zero-trust intent layer between AI agents and their tools. 

 The goal is to make sure every action stays within the limits defined by the human. 

 What it does 

 MIRROR turns a human instruction into an Intent Contract that defines what an agent can and cannot do. 

 For example: 

 
 "Research development laptops under $1,200. Compare them. Do not purchase anything." 
 

 MIRROR converts this into: 

 
 Allowed: search_products , get_product_details , compare_products 
 Denied: purchase_product 
 Approval Required: actions that need human approval 
 

 Every tool request is checked before execution. 

 MIRROR returns: 
 ALLOW
APPROVAL_REQUIRED
DENY
 
 It also records information such as: 
 Risk
Intent Drift
Reason Codes
Timestamp
 
 How I built it 

 Backend: Python, Django, Django REST Framework 

 Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite 

 Database: PostgreSQL, Supabase 

 Deployment: Cloudflare Pages, Render, Supabase 

 WebMCP: Used real WebMCP tool registration and discovery to expose executable web capabilities. 

 Challenges i ran into 

 Building a Real Authorization Boundary 

 The main challenge was making MIRROR an actual security layer rather than just a dashboard. 

 Tool requests are evaluated by the backend before the action is allowed to continue. 

 WebMCP Integration 

 I needed to connect real WebMCP capabilities with MIRROR's authorization system. 

 The application uses: 
 document . modelContext . registerTool ( . . . ) 
 
 and: 
 document . modelContext . getTools ( ) 
 
 Keeping Security Decisions Clear 

 Different tools can have different risks. 

 I needed one clear decision format that could explain why an action was allowed or blocked. 

 Example: 
 {
 "decision": "DENY",
 "drift_score": 0.87,
 "reason_codes": [
 "INTENT_VIOLATION"
 ]
}
 
 Accomplishments that i was proud of 

 
 Built a working Intent Contract system. 
 Added bounded authority for agents. 
 Integrated real WebMCP tools . 
 Added ALLOW , APPROVAL_REQUIRED , and DENY decisions. 
 Added intent-drift scoring and risk classification. 
 Added activity and audit logging. 
 Built a live security dashboard. 
 Deployed the project publicly. 
 

 The main demonstration is simple: 
 Human:
"Do not purchase anything."

Agent:
purchase_product

MIRROR:
DENY
 
 The current prototype demonstrates unauthorized requests being blocked in under 100ms . 

 What i learned 

 The biggest lesson was: 

 
 Capability is not authorization. 
 

 An agent can be capable of performing an action without being authorized to perform it. 

 I also learned that: 

 
 Human intent needs to become structured policy before it can be enforced. 
 Authorization should remain separate from the agent's own reasoning. 
 Security decisions should be visible and explainable. 
 WebMCP makes agent capabilities more structured and easier to control. 
 

 What's Next for MIRROR 

 MIRROR is designed as a foundation for a broader security control plane for autonomous web agents. 

 Future versions could extend the current intent-and-authority model with: 

 
 Cryptographically Signed Intent Contracts - prevent unauthorized modification of an agent's approved intent. 
 Fine-Grained Data Permissions - control not only which tools an agent can use, but which data fields and resources it can access. 
 One-Time Approval Tokens - allow humans to authorize a specific high-risk action without granting permanent permission. 
 Agent-to-Agent Authorization - enforce trust boundaries when one agent delegates work to another. 
 Policy Simulation - preview how a proposed agent action would be evaluated before execution. 
 Advanced Semantic Intent-Drift Detection - use semantic analysis to detect when an agent's requested action gradually diverges from the user's original goal. 
 SDKs for Agent Frameworks - make MIRROR easy to integrate into different autonomous-agent stacks. 
 

 The long-term goal is to make MIRROR a reusable zero-trust security control plane for autonomous web agents , where an agent's capabilities are never treated as authorization by themselves. 

 Why WebMCP? 

 WebMCP gives agents structured access to web capabilities. 

 MIRROR adds the authorization layer around those capabilities. 
 WebMCP
"What can this website do?"

MIRROR
"What is this agent allowed to do?"
 
 This makes WebMCP a natural fit for MIRROR because tools are explicit, discoverable, and machine-readable. 

 
 WebMCP defines capability. MIRROR defines authority. 
 

 Potential Impact 

 As agents gain the ability to: 
 purchase
book
send
submit
modify
transact
 
 they also need stronger authorization controls. 

 MIRROR explores a model where users can give agents autonomy without giving them unrestricted power . 

 The human defines the boundaries. 

 The agent performs the work. 

 MIRROR enforces the boundaries.

 Built for the OpenAI WebMCP Challenge 

 MIRROR was built for the OpenAI WebMCP Challenge to explore safer interaction between humans, AI agents, and the web. 

 The project uses WebMCP as a real capability layer and adds a separate authorization layer based on human intent, bounded authority, and explainable decisions . 

 
 Capability is not authorization.

 Zero-Trust Policy Engine: Designed and implemented a server-side evaluation engine in Python and Django REST Framework that intercepts agent tool calls prior to execution, evaluating requests against active rules to return sub-100ms enforcement decisions (ALLOW, APPROVAL_REQUIRED, DENY). 

 Intent Contract & Bounded Authority Model: Developed the translation pipeline converting natural-language human instructions into structured, machine-enforceable policy contracts containing strict least-authority boundaries and override rules. 

 Real-Time Intent Drift & Telemetry System: Implemented a dynamic intent drift scoring algorithm ($0.00$ to $1.00$) and an immutable audit logging pipeline that records evaluation decisions, assigned risk levels, reason codes, and execution timestamps. 

 WebMCP Protocol Integration: Built native WebMCP protocol hooks (document.modelContext.registerTool, getTools, and executeTool) to bridge tool discovery with server-side
